note: About the icon a browser shows for a web page. An app sets its window and tray icons itself.
Inline `<svg>` and SVG images draw with lib-svg: shapes, paths, text, gradients, patterns, clipping, masks and markers.
In icons: lib-svg draws `<filter>` elements with every primitive.
App text cannot use SVG fonts: `@font-face` does not load them. Inside an icon's markup, lib-svg draws the document's own `<font>` elements.
An icon draws its whole document; a `#id` or `#svgView(...)` fragment in its URL does not pick out a part.

Nodes cannot use SVG effects by reference: `filter: url(#id)` is skipped, `clip-path: url(#id)` clips to the border box, and there is no `foreignObject` for nodes. CSS filter functions, shapes and gradient masks work.

Inline `<svg>` markup works in React, Foldkit and plain JavaScript (`createSvgElement`, or `document.createElementNS` after importing `@silkui/core/globals`); markup held as a string goes in as a `data:image/svg+xml` image. An `<svg>` drawn once and then changed updates element by element, redrawing only the shapes that changed, so script animations such as stock lottie-web play. Listeners on its elements hear pointer events on their shapes, and `getBBox()`, `getTotalLength()` and `getPointAtLength()` work. The whole `<svg>` is one node: its elements take attributes and `style`, not app stylesheets, and `foreignObject` is not drawn.

An image node draws an `.svg` file or a `data:image/svg+xml` URL (base64 or percent-encoded), as `` does, at the file's own `width` and `height` when CSS gives no size. Unlike ``, its `currentColor` is the node's `color`.
SMIL and CSS animations inside an icon play, rendered per frame. Good for small icons such as spinners; each frame is a separate texture.
